findings.title: CI 7-day cooldown checker silently skips every pin carrying an inline comment
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/release.yml 'Dependency release-age cooldown (7d)' step: lines are processed as `line.split(';')[0].strip()` (strips environment markers only) then matched with `^([A-Za-z0-9_.\-]+)==([\w.\-]+)$` which requires end-of-line after the version. All 6 pins in requirements-ml.txt carry inline `# [V] ...` comments (faster-whisper==1.2.1, ctranslate2==4.8.5, onnxruntime==1.31.1, av==18.1.0, tokenizers==0.23.3, huggingface-hub==0.36.2) -> ALL are silently excluded; the job prints 'checked N pins' without flagging skips. The one new clean pin (websocket-client==1.9.2) IS checked.
findings.current_state_verification: No present violation: every requirements*.txt pin is >= 7 days old (in-file [V] date evidence; auditor independently verified websocket-client==1.9.2 upload time 2026-08-31 via PyPI JSON = ~78d).
findings.impact: A future dependency change written with an inline comment bypasses the automated cooldown gate entirely, defeating policy rules/01 s20 / I2 enforcement-by-default.
findings.minimal_fix: Strip inline comments before matching: `line = line.split('#')[0].split(';')[0].strip()`, and count/print skipped non-empty pin-like lines instead of silently ignoring them. Optionally fail when 0 pins match.
findings.mandate: Fix REQUIRED before the next dependency addition/upgrade (tracked as HN-DICT-03). If release policy treats CI gate soundness as blocking in itself, escalate verdict to FAIL.

findings.title: U2 Gemini consent gate does not cover stage-2 cleanup / Polish cloud cleanup routed to the google-gemini chat preset
findings.evidence: dictation_session.preflight gates Gemini only at the documented U2 enforcement points (chunked engine resolved == 'google-gemini' :216-217; live engine gemini-live :386-387; plan/A3 proposal scope = 'Gemini engines'). But cleanup_mode='cloud' stage-2 (chunked_engine._cleanup -> llm_api.post_process_text with api_keys[provider_id]) and polish_engine.polish_last cloud path send the FULL TRANSCRIPT to the current chat provider; providers registry contains a selectable 'google-gemini' preset (providers.py:98). Free-tier training exposure is exactly the risk U2 gates (A6 proposal V2c).
findings.exploitable_today: User must select google-gemini as chat provider themselves; the same flow pre-exists in the classic pipeline (accepted at the provider-presets gate) and is arguably user-elected. No attacker input required.
findings.impact: Transcript reaches Google free tier (may train) without the red consent disclosure gate that the live/chunked Gemini ENGINES require.
findings.minimal_fix: Extend _require_gemini_consent to the cleanup stage when providers.resolve_provider_id(provider) == 'google-gemini' (local + chunked modes and polish_last cloud path), or state the cleanup exposure in the consent copy.

findings.title: model_store post-install verification result is discarded; pre-existing files activate on presence-only
findings.evidence: model_store.py:203 calls self._reverify(model_id, version_dir) and ignores its return value before self._activate(...) at :204, contradicting the adjacent comment ('re-hash installed bytes before activation — never trusted on the file name alone'). Also :182-185: when all manifest files are present (any content), _download_one activates without digest verification (by-design bounded boot: _refresh_installed checks presence+size only; full hashing is the user-triggered re_check_file).
findings.reasoning: Pre-rename digest+size gate (:265) already guarantees pinned bytes at install time; changing files afterwards requires local same-user write access to the model store dir (D1 client-trust: such an attacker can edit any app file). Network/manifest adversaries cannot reach this state.
findings.minimal_fix: raise _StoreError('failed', ...) when _reverify returns False at :203 (one line).

findings.title: LLKHF_INJECTED self-filter cannot distinguish own vs foreign injected keys; WM_CHAR/PostMessage text never hits the hook
findings.evidence: focus_guard.py:247-255 filters info.flags & LLKHF_INJECTED; the flag is set by win32k for EVERY process's SendInput output, so a background automation tool (AutoHotkey, clipboard managers, IME helpers) typing into the target document does NOT invalidate polish spans, and text delivered via WM_CHAR/PostMessage never reaches WH_KEYBOARD_LL at all. Docstring (:17-18) over-claims 'OUR OWN SendInput output'.
findings.exploitable_today: Requires a same-user background automation process editing the same document (D1 local attacker class) AND the user later invoking polish replace-experimental / select-back.
findings.impact_bounded_by: default polish_mode='insert' (no select-back), replace-experimental opt-in + on_windows + focus_unchanged PROOF + 10-min TTL + span invalidated by every physical key + spans registered only after successful injection + auto-fallback to insert on any doubt.
findings.minimal_fix: Correct the docstring; optionally compare dwExtraInfo to a per-session magic marker set on our SendInput events (still spoofable by same-user code) — or accept and document.

findings.title: Focus guard check -> SendInput micro-race can misdeliver at most one emission
findings.evidence: typer_actor.guarded_emit (:146-178) checks focus then sends the phrase; a window switch between check() and the SendInput batch lands that one phrase in the new foreground window. SendInput cannot atomically bind to a target hwnd (inherent platform TOCTOU).
findings.impact_bounded_by: per-emission re-check (next emission raises FocusLostError and is RETAINED for resume/copy); abort/is_exiting double-check; one phrase maximum per race.

findings.title: SessionClipboard is not restored when the app exits mid-session
findings.evidence: typer_actor.stop (:110-113) skips clipboard.close()/restore when is_exiting (M2: zero clipboard ops during teardown). The pre-session clipboard is therefore not restored on quit; the retained-backlog copy is also skipped.
findings.impact_bounded_by: deliberate M2 contract; normal close() uses the equality guard so a newer user copy is never clobbered; loss is the pre-session clipboard value only.
